candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Berlin sculptor stages steel-and-stone benches in the Prison Yard, collapsing waiting rooms into monuments.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Site-specific installation by major contemporary artist

candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: First major Egyptian loan show to Hong Kong tests appetite for civilizational narratives beyond the Sinosphere.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: Met jewellery survey examining adornment across cultures; Hong Kong as a natural staging ground for luxury taxonomy.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Convergence of luxury, anthropology, Asia hub

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Private Western collector's Chinese textiles recontextualised in Hong Kong, probing taste, trade, and custodianship.

candidates.title: Joyful Encounters: The Connoisseurship and Art of Wong Kwan Shut
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong scholar-painter whose late Qing revival circles map a forgotten modernism between tradition and treaty port.

candidates.title: Heavenly Horses: Masterpieces from the Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Imperial equine iconography spanning Tang ceramics to Qing armour, tracing military power and pastoral fantasy.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong's 61st Venice Biennale collateral pavilion returns home, double-framing the city's biennial ambitions.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Rare opportunity to see HK Venice show locally

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Survey of contemporary Hong Kong practice; title suggests performance or durational work beyond static display.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Potential live programme, local scene focus

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Export porcelain and trade paintings that defined global China taste, now viewed through Pearl River Delta lens.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Canton trade history, HK as inheritor

candidates.title: Brilliance: Ming Dynasty Ceramic Treasures from the Palace Museum, 1368–1644
candidates.blurb: Long-run Ming ceramics show positions Hong Kong as semi-permanent ceramics study centre.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: The Forbidden City and the World — Cultural Encounters
candidates.blurb: Two-year thematic rotation on Qing court's global entanglements; Hong Kong as decoder of imperial cosmopolitanism.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Multi-year thematic anchor, HK as interpreter

candidates.title: The Adorned Body: French Fashion and Jewellery 1770–1910 from the Musée des Arts Décoratifs, Paris
candidates.blurb: French decorative arts positioned against Palace Museum holdings, testing dialogue or incongruity.
